legacy: Robert Millikan helped establish modern experimental physics through exceptionally precise measurements that strengthened understanding of atomic structure and electrical phenomena. His work demonstrated the power of careful experimentation and made quantitative measurement a central feature of twentieth-century physics. His influence extended beyond research through his efforts to improve science education and scientific institutions.
earlyLife: Millikan was born in Illinois and grew up in a family that valued education, discipline, and intellectual development. Initially interested in mathematics and teaching, he gradually became attracted to physics through academic study and laboratory work. His early experiences convinced him that scientific progress depended upon accurate measurement and rigorous experimentation.
scientificField: Physics, Experimental Physics, Atomic Physics, Electromagnetism
majorContribution: Millikan is best known for determining the elementary electric charge through a series of highly controlled experiments involving tiny charged droplets. His work provided strong evidence for the discrete nature of electric charge and contributed to the development of modern atomic theory. He also conducted influential studies of the photoelectric effect and helped refine key physical constants through precise measurement.
laterLife: During his later career, Millikan became a leading scientific administrator and public advocate for scientific literacy. He held influential academic positions, promoted research institutions, and worked to increase public appreciation of scientific knowledge. His lectures and writings helped make physics more accessible to students and general audiences alike.
whyImportant: Millikan played a vital role in confirming fundamental properties of matter through experimental evidence. His measurements strengthened the foundations of modern physics and provided essential data for future advances in atomic and quantum science. His commitment to precision set standards that continue to guide scientific research today.
